newsitem.title: FRANCE: French colonel denies recruiting Zaire mercenaries.
newsitem.headline: French colonel denies recruiting Zaire mercenaries.

text.p: A former chief of security at the French presidency has denied that he is putting together a mercenary force to help the government of Zaire fight Rwandan-backed rebels.
"It's not in my work methods to employ mercenaries," Alain Le Carro, a colonel in the para-military gendarmerie who left the service in 1994, told the conservative daily Le Figaro.
He dismissed a report in Tuesday's Le Monde that he was in eastern Zaire assembling a "White Legion" of several hundred European and African mercenaries.

Le Carro said he was neither directly nor indirectly involved. "Furthermore, I'm in Paris and not in Zaire, as Le Monde claims," he said, adding he had never had ties to Zaire's leaders and had not even visited the country since 1982.

Le Carro, head of the presidential guard at the Elysee palace during late Socialist president Francois Mitterrand's rule, said he worked as an advisor to the governments of Burkina Faso and the Ivory Coast.

Le Monde alleged that Le Carro was working in Zaire with another former gendarme, Robert Montoya, who carried out anti-terrorism missions for the presidency and was involved in a wiretap scandal before leaving the service 10 years ago.
Le Figaro said that a lawyer for Montoya, the only other French officer named in Le Monde's report, had also denied any involvement in recruiting mercenaries.

Le Monde said the force numbered between 200 and 300 but was expected to grow rapidly when more men leave Europe in two weeks to join South African, French, Belgian, British, Angolan and Mozambican soldiers of fortune on the spot.

On Tuesday, French Cooperation Minister Jacques Godfrain said there were mercenaries from some European nations in the region but denied any official French involvement, saying Paris was the victim of a media smear campaign.

The French presidency said it had no connection with, or knowledge of, a mercenary force. France backs Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko politically but an international arms embargo on Zaire bars any military aid.
